NOTE:  PUBLIC PARTICIPATION INFORMATION
  In accordance with Assembly Bill 361 (AB 361) and City Council Resolution No. 2487, due to the
  continuing state of emergency, including masking and social distancing directives as a result of the threat
  of the COVID-19 virus, this meeting is being held remotely via teleconference. There will not be a physical
  location for this meeting. Members of the public may participate in the meeting in the following ways:

  - Members of the public may listen to the meeting live by calling: (1 669 900 6833) from any phone,
  Meeting ID: 875 0650 1816 Meeting Password: 066081. (Please note you will not have the ability to
  speak using the call in option from a phone line.)

  - Public correspondence may be emailed to the City Clerk at laurenp@rollinghillsestatesca.gov. Emails
  received before 3:00 p.m. prior to the start of the meeting will be forwarded to the City Council for their
  consideration and included as part of the record.

  - Members of the public may also comment online using eComment on the “Meeting Agendas, Minutes &
  Videos” page of the City’s website (www.rhe.city/MeetingAgendas). Once the agenda is published, there
  will be an “eComment” button next to the linked agenda under "Upcoming Events". Follow this link to
  the City’s SpeakUp page. After you register, you may comment on any item on that particular agenda.
  These comments can be seen by the public, will be considered by the Council and become part of the
  record.

  - Members of the public who wish to speak during this meeting may join the Zoom meeting by accessing the
  Zoom app from a computer (downloaded at Zoom.com) or tablet or phone (downloaded in the App Store),
  by entering the following credentials: Meeting ID: 875 0650 1816, Meeting Password: 066081. Members
  of the public who join the Zoom meeting will not have video, and may request to speak using the following
  process: After joining the Zoom meeting, if you wish to speak, please select the "raise hand" option at the
  lower portion of your screen. The City Clerk will send you a chat message to identify which item on the
  agenda you would like to speak on and will unmute your mic at the appropriate time.

  Agenda reports and other disclosable public records relating to each Open Session agenda item are
  available on the City's website under Meeting Agendas, Minutes & Videos at www.rhe.city.

MINUTES
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  NOVEMBER 9, 2021

1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

A regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to order
by MAYOR ZUCKERMAN at 7:01 pm remotely via teleconference, in accordance with
Assembly Bill 361 (AB 361) and City Council Resolution No. 2487, due to the continuing
state of emergency, including masking and social distancing directives as a result of the
threat of the COVID-19 virus.

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

Led by MAYOR ZUCKERMAN.

3.  ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman

City Council Members Absent:  None

City Staff Present:  City Manager Greg Grammer
  City Attorney Don Davis
  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis
  Administrative Services Director Mike Whitehead
  Community Development & PW Director David Wahba
  Planning Manager Naughton
  City Clerk Lauren Pettit
  Management Analyst Jessica Slawson

4.  CEREMONIAL ITEMS

A.  PROCLAMATION: DECLARING NOVEMBER 27, 2021 AS "SMALL BUSINESS
  SATURDAY"

MAYOR ZUCKERMAN declared November 27, 2021 Small Business Saturday.

B.  WASTE MANAGEMENT "RECYCLING HERO" DRAWING FOR ONE YEAR OF FREE
  RESIDENTIAL AND COMMERCIAL REFUSE SERVICE - FOURTH QUARTER 2021

On behalf of Waste Management, Sharon Shapiro Fox provided an update on WM’s holiday
collection schedule. She also drew names for the fourth quarter “Recycling Hero” winners of
one year of free refuse service.

  RESIDENTIAL WINNER: 139 Cottonwood Circle
  COMMERCIAL WINNER: Mail Shop Etc. 904 Silver Spur Road

5.  CONSENT CALENDAR

The following routine matters will be acted upon by one vote to approve with the majority
consent of the City Council. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless good
cause is shown by a member prior to the roll call vote. (Items removed for individual
consideration will be voted on separately.)

  COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN,
  TO APPROVE CONSENT CALENDAR ITEMS 5A-I AS FOLLOWS BY THE
  FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  1
NOVEMBER 9, 2021
 A.  READING OF ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS BY TITLE ONLY

  APPROVED.

B.  DEMANDS AND WARRANTS OF OCTOBER & NOVEMBER 2021

  APPROVED WARRANTS 64445 THROUGH 64481 IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $482,152.64 AND SUPPLEMENTAL WARRANTS 100421 THROUGH
  100521 IN THE AMOUNT OF $79,362.30 FOR A GRAND TOTAL AMOUNT
  OF $561,514.94 WITH PROPER AUDIT.

C.  BUDGET AMENDMENT FISCAL YEAR 2020-2021

  APPROVED AS PRESENTED.

**COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ abstained from voting on Item 5D.

D.  CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF OCTOBER 26, 2021

  REVIEWED AND APPROVED.

E.  PARK & ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MINUTES OF OCTOBER 18, 2021

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

F.  EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES OF OCTOBER 25, 2021

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

G.  ENVIRONMENTAL ADVISORY COMMITTEE MINUTES OF OCTOBER 27, 2021

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

H.  PLANNING COMMISSION MINUTES OF NOVEMBER 1, 2021

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

I.  ADOPTION OF RESOLUTION 2490 TO AUTHORIZE THE USE OF
  TELECONFERENCE ACCESSIBILITY PROCEDURES TO CONDUCT PUBLIC
  MEETINGS PURSUANT TO ASSEMBLY BILL 361

  ADOPTED RESOLUTION 2490 TO AUTHORIZE THE CITY MANAGER TO
  IMPLEMENT AND UTILIZE TELECONFERENCE ACCESSIBILITY
  PROCEDURES TO CONDUCT PUBLIC MEETINGS PURSUANT TO
  ASSEMBLY BILL 361.

6.  PUBLIC COMMENT / PUBLIC PRESENTATIONS

NONE.

7.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

NONE.

8.  NEW BUSINESS

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ moved to adjourn to the Pepper Tree Foundation
  Board meeting, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF.

**ADJOURN TO PEPPER TREE FOUNDATION BOARD MEETING**

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
NOVEMBER 9, 2021
 A.  ESTABLISHMENT OF PEPPER TREE FOUNDATION FUNDRAISING COMMITTEE

  Recommendation: That the Board of Directors review the development of a fundraising
  committee and provide staff direction on how to proceed with the composition and
  associated recruitment.

Assistant City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF suggested the committee be made up of Council Members, as
discussed during the Policy Development Session (PDS) meeting in March 2021.

City Attorney Davis stated that there are no legal restrictions for a Council Member to do the
proposed functions of this Committee, in response to COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ. He
stated that staff is recommending the Council have a liaison/oversight position over the
Committee.

Discussion ensued regarding options for the role of Council Members within the Committee.

City Manager Grammer summarized that staff proposes that the City Council and Park and
Activities Commission, serving as the Board and Advisory Board to the Pepper Tree
Foundation, would continue in their role of approving projects and identifying fundraising needs,
while the new Fundraising Committee would go out into the community and actively fundraise.

MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN suggested the Council not be included as members on the
Committee and suggested involving former Council Members and other prominent members
of the community to volunteer on the Committee.

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF emphasized including prominent members of the business
community as well.

City Attorney Davis noted that behested payments have a reporting requirement of above
$5,000 for a single donation or $5,000 within a cumulative year from a single source, in
response to MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN.

Assistant City Manager Davis confirmed recruitment would begin with Council Members doing
outreach and connecting with staff, formally announcing Committee Members to the Board in
January during the Foundation’s annual report.

Public comment was invited via email, via eComment on the City’s website, and during the live
Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website and social media platforms.
No public testimony was received.

  CONSENSUS OF THE COUNCIL TO ESTABLISH A PEPPER TREE
  FOUNDATION FUNDRAISING COMMITTEE CONSISTING OF UP TO 8
  MEMBERS OF THE COMMUNITY.

There being no objection, MAYOR ZUCKERMAN so ordered.

  COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA moved to adjourn the Pepper Tree Foundation
  Board meeting and reconvene the City Council meeting, seconded by COUNCIL
  MEMBER HUFF.

**RECONVENE TO CITY COUNCIL MEETING**

B.  BEHESTED PAYMENT POLICY

  Recommendation: That the City Council review and approve the proposed Behested
  Payment Policy.

City Attorney Davis provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

City Attorney Davis explained that although the contents of this policy are already required
by State law, they are spread across many different regulations so it is helpful to have a

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
NOVEMBER 9, 2021
 consolidated City policy, as requested by the Council at the Policy Development Session, in
response to COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA.

Public comment was invited via email, via eComment on the City’s website, and during the live
Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website and social media platforms.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM
  ZERUNYAN, AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  APPROVE THE PROPOSED BEHESTED PAYMENT POLICY.

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

C.  PARK & ACTIVITIES COMMISSION ACTION ITEM: 2021 CITY CELEBRATION
  DEBRIEFING

  Recommendation: That City Council provide input to staff and the City Celebration
  Subcommittee in the planning and budgeting of the 65th Annual City Celebration
  scheduled to be held in September 2022 at the Empty Saddle Club.

Assistant City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF commended staff for their work on the event, and suggested
staff consider purchasing a canopy to be used for future events.

Assistant City Manager Davis clarified that the sound system rental line item included the
cost of the DJ, in response to COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA.

MAYOR ZUCKERMAN stated he was pleased the event was successful and well attended.

COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ commended staff for its victory in the annual volleyball
match with Lomita Sheriff’s Station.

Public comment was invited via email, via eComment on the City’s website, and during the live
Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website and social media platforms.
No public testimony was received.

Consensus of the Council to receive and file the report.

D.  PARK & ACTIVITIES COMMISSION ACTION ITEM: PUBLIC RIDING RING RULES
  REVIEW - CHANDLER ARENA

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve a temporary update to the Riding
  Ring Rules eliminating the restriction of training hours established on weekends and
  National holidays at Chandler Arena as identified in Resolution No. 2334, Section 2
  (K).

Assistant City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

Assistant City Manager Davis stated that the Equestrian Committee brought forth this
request after seeing how trainers were impacted, in response to COUNCIL MEMBER
SCHMITZ.

Park and Activities Commissioner and Equestrian Committee representative Valerie Ciarolla
summarized the requests she has heard from the equestrian community to make this
change.

COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ requested that analytics be collected during this period to
help evaluate the change at the end of the trial period.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
NOVEMBER 9, 2021
 COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA inquired if members of the public were surveyed to see if
they mind using the riding ring along with the trainers. Assistant City Manager Davis stated
that the Equestrian Committee Members are all recreation riders, and are very supportive of
the change.

Assistant City Manager Davis also noted that staff will have a survey available at the arena,
and will do outreach periodically throughout the six-month trial for feedback.

Public comment was invited via email, via eComment on the City’s website, and during the live
Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website and social media platforms.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF,
  TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  APPROVE A TEMPORARY UPDATE TO THE RIDING RING RULES
  ELIMINATING THE RESTRICTION OF TRAINING HOURS ESTABLISHED ON
  WEEKENDS AND NATIONAL HOLIDAYS AT CHANDLER ARENA AS
  IDENTIFIED IN RESOLUTION NO. 2334, SECTION 2 (K).

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

E.  ENVIRONMENTAL ADVISORY COMMITTEE ACTION ITEM: ZERO EMISSION
  VEHICLE PROCUREMENT

  Recommendation: That City Council approve the purchase of a 2022 Chevrolet Bolt
  EV 5dr Wagon 1LT at the cost of $30,073.75 funded in part by the South Coast Air
  Quality Management District (SCQAMD) Mobile Source Air Pollutions Reductions
  reimbursable grant in the amount of $10,000; the remaining balance of $20,073.74
  will be funded by the General Fund, as allocated in the FY 2021-22 Budget.

Assistant City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ inquired about the recent recall related to battery fires in the
Chevrolet Bolt.

Discussion ensued about recent recalls from Chevrolet and the Environmental Advisory
Committee’s discussion regarding these recalls.

Assistant City Manager Davis noted that there is time to further research this item, in relation
to the AQMD grant deadline.

Assistant City Manager Davis also noted that this will be a highly used vehicle among several
departments, in response to COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF.

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA noted that the Environmental Advisory Committee
discussed the benefit of staff not using personal vehicles with personally identifiable
characteristics, protecting staff as they go out into the community.

Public comment was invited via email, via eComment on the City’s website, and during the live
Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website and social media platforms.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF,
  TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  DIRECT STAFF TO FURTHER RESEARCH THE RECENT CHEVROLET
  BOLT BATTERY RECALL, AND BRING THIS INFORMATION BACK TO THE
  COUNCIL IN DECEMBER FOR CONSIDERATION AND APPROVAL.

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  5
NOVEMBER 9, 2021
 F.  ENVIRONMENTAL ADVISORY COMMITTEE ACTION ITEM: CHARGE READY 2
  PROGRAM UPDATE

  Recommendation: That the City Council consider the installation of six (6) dual port
  electric vehicle (EV) charging stations located at City Hall and direct staff to return
  with 1) an Agreement to participate in Southern California Edison’s Charge Ready 2
  Program for EV infrastructure and 2) final quotes for the purchase of six dual port
  electric vehicle stations.

Assistant City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

Assistant City Manager Davis explained that combustion vehicles will not be prohibited from
parking in Electric Vehicle (EV) charging stations, in response to COUNCIL MEMBER
SCHMITZ. She also noted that if needed for a specific event, signage can be posted to make
clear that any vehicle can use the EV parking spots.

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA confirmed that the required number of ADA parking spots
will remain in the parking lot, with the addition of these six EV charging stations.

Public comment was invited via email, via eComment on the City’s website, and during the live
Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website and social media platforms.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF,
  TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  APPROVE THE INSTALLATION OF SIX (6) DUAL PORT ELECTRIC VEHICLE
  (EV) CHARGING STATIONS LOCATED AT CITY HALL AND DIRECT STAFF
  TO RETURN WITH 1) AN AGREEMENT TO PARTICIPATE IN SOUTHERN
  CALIFORNIA EDISON’S CHARGE READY 2 PROGRAM FOR EV

C.  SECOND READING AND ADOPTION OF ORDINANCE NO. 736 AMENDING AND
  RESTATING CHAPTER 10.44 OF THE ROLLING HILLS ESTATES MUNICIPAL
  CODE PERTAINING TO THE REGULATION OF BICYCLES, ELECTRIC BICYCLES,
  AND MOTORIZED BICYCLES

  Recommendation: That the City Council conduct the second reading, and adopt
  Ordinance No. 736.

Management Analyst Slawson provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN noted that many residents in the Dapplegray neighborhood
use electric bicycles (e-bikes) to drop-off and pick-up their children from school. He discussed
the queuing of cars along Palos Verdes Drive North during the school drop-off and pick-up
times, and emphasized that e-bikes help remove additional vehicles from the roads in the City.

Discussion ensued about the multi-use pathway along Palos Verdes Drive North, and the use
of this pathway by e-bikes during high-traffic hours when cars queue along the right side of
Palos Verdes Drive North and block the bike lane.

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF and COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ agreed with MAYOR PRO
TEM ZERUNYAN.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  6
NOVEMBER 9, 2021
 COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ stated that she thinks e-bikes are an innovative way for
families to transport their children to and from school that it is better for the environment and
helps alleviate traffic.

MAYOR ZUCKERMAN stated that the use of e-bikes on sidewalks are problematic. City
Attorney Davis noted that there currently is no regulation of e-bikes, but the proposed
Ordinance would prohibit the use of e-bikes on sidewalks.

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA noted safety concerns regarding the use of e-bikes on the
multi-use pathway, as well as the challenges of enforcement of any e-bike regulations. She
suggested the possibility of designating a marked bike-zone and pedestrian-zone in the school
zones of the multi-use pathway. MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN stated that he did not think
there would be enough space to designate different zones.

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA stated that she does not believe the answer is no regulation
of e-bikes.

COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ stated that we cannot legislate for good manners.

Discussion ensued about the addition of a speed limit, the challenges of enforcement, and
regulating differently for the different classes of e-bikes.

Public comment was invited via email, via eComment on the City’s website, and during the live
Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website and social media platforms.
Public testimony was received from residents Dan Smith, Syu, and Bridget Carman in
opposition of the ordinance.

City Attorney Davis summarized that staff is looking for direction on which classes of e-bikes
to exempt, if any, and clarification on the use of e-bikes on the multi-use pathway.

  MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER

  COMMUNITY, AND BRING BACK A NEW ORDINANCE AT A FUTURE
  COUNCIL MEETING.

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None
